q: If an entry fails to meet the ADC's mandatory requirements, instructions, or Conditions, what action must the Jury take?
o: Disqualify it
Award it a reduced honorarium
Ask the Competitor to revise and resubmit it
Refer it to the IAPOA ADC Committee for a final ruling
n: The Jury shall disqualify any design which does not conform to the mandatory requirements, instructions or Conditions for the ADC. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.11)

q: For a two-stage competition, under what circumstance can the names of those advancing to the second stage be disclosed?
o: Right after the first-stage results, in the interest of transparency
Only under exceptional conditions the Jury agreed on before the ADC was launched
Never, under any circumstance
Only after the Owner secures the IAPOA President's written consent
n: The names of those Competitors selected to proceed to the second stage of a two-stage competition shall be made public only under exceptional conditions to be agreed on by the Jury before the launching of the ADC. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 10.3)

q: What kind of line must the ADC Conditions draw regarding what competitors submit?
o: Local vs. foreign competitors
Digital vs. physical submissions
Mandatory requirements vs. free interpretation
Individual vs. firm entries
n: A clear distinction shall be made between the mandatory requirements of the Competition and those which permit the competitor freedom of interpretation, and all entries must be submitted in the manner prescribed in the Conditions. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.4)

q: Is it permissible for a Jury member to enter the competition himself, or later be commissioned to work on the winning design?
o: Yes, if he abstains on his own entry
Yes, if the Owner approves
Yes, but only in invitational ADCs
No, not directly or indirectly
n: No member of the Jury will be allowed to take part in the competition, either directly or indirectly, nor be commissioned with work connected with the prize-winning design either directly or indirectly. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 7.1)

q: Once the ADC results are in, what is the Owner required to do concerning the registered Competitors and the IAPOA?
o: Notify all entrants and IAPOA, with the jury report
Wait until the exhibition closes
Notify only the winner
Publish only in the Official Gazette
n: The Owner shall notify in a timely manner all registered Competitors of the date and place of the public exhibition and the results of the ADC, and send them a copy of the Jury's report. He shall similarly inform the IAPOA, and photographs of the prize-winning designs shall be sent to the IAPOA with an option for publication. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 12.2)

q: For an ADC, who names and compensates the Professional Advisor, and whose approval does that appointment require?
o: IAPOA, with no approval needed
The Owner, with IAPOA NBD approval
The competitors, with the Owner's OK
The Jury, with Secretariat approval
n: A Professional Advisor should be appointed and paid by the Owner and approved by the IAPOA National Board of Directors (NBD) through its ADC Committee. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 5.1)

q: What narrower prize scheme does SPP Document 208 allow specifically for an Ideas Competition?
o: Prize money split evenly among every entrant
Only in-kind prizes, with no cash awards
It may be permissible to compensate only the first-prize winner
No prize may be awarded at all
n: It is important for the Owner to allot adequate prize money to compensate all the Competitors for their work; however, for an Ideas Competition only, it may be possible to remunerate only the first (1st) prize winner. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.2)

q: From start to the final prize-giving, who holds sole arbiter status at every stage of the ADC?
o: The IAPOA ADC Committee
The Owner's board of directors
The Professional Advisor
The Jury members
n: The Jury members are the sole arbiters at all stages, up to the final prize-giving. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 14.2)

q: At what point must an ADC's Jury be constituted, and in what document must its members' (and reserves') names appear?
o: Before the competition is officially announced, with names stated in the Conditions
Only once the second stage begins, named in a separate memorandum
At the Professional Advisor's own discretion, listed in the exhibition catalogue
After the competition has closed, listed in the Jury's final report
n: The Jury shall be set up before the official announcement of the competition, and the names of the Jury and its reserve members shall be stated in the Conditions. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.1)

q: What payment goes to Competitors advancing to a two-stage competition's second round, and what is it meant to cover?
o: A refund of the first-stage fee
An honorarium for the extra second-stage work
A share of the Advisor's fee
Nothing beyond the eventual prize
n: In two-stage competitions, Competitors selected to take part in the second stage shall be paid a reasonable honorarium, stated in the Conditions, in addition to the prizes awarded, to reimburse them for the additional work carried out in the second stage. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.5)

q: Broadly speaking, what does SPP Document 208 deal with, as part of the profession's Standards of Professional Practice?
o: The scale of design fees in general
CPD requirements for architects
The conduct of architectural design competitions
The licensure exam syllabus
n: SPP Document 208 (part of the 2010 Standards of Professional Practice) sets out the rules governing Architectural Design Competitions — the roles of the Owner, Jury, Professional Advisor, and IAPOA ADC Committee, the drawing up of Conditions, prizes and honoraria, copyright and ownership, registration of competitors, insurance, exhibitions, return of projects, and alternative dispute resolution. (Source: SPP Document 208 (2010 Standards of Professional Practice), generally)

q: Beyond the seven-member cap, what other numerical rule governs how the Jury is composed?
o: It must be divisible by three
It must be an even number, to allow tie-breaking votes
There is no other numerical rule
It must be an odd number
n: The Jury shall be composed of the smallest reasonable number of persons and in any event should be an odd number, not exceeding seven (7). (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.3)

q: Per the scenario, since no design/build contract materializes within the Conditions' allotted period, what must SPP Document 208 pay out to the first-prize winner, and when does that obligation kick in?
o: A further sum equal to the first prize, after 12 months
Double the prize, after 6 months
Nothing beyond the first prize
10% of the project cost, after 3 months
n: In Project ADCs, provisions shall be made in the Conditions for the first prize winner to receive compensation of a further sum equal to the amount of the first prize (here, another PHP 500,000) if no contract is signed within twelve (12) months of the announcement of the Jury's award. The Owner still does not acquire the right to carry out the project except with the Author's collaboration. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.8)
scenario: A Project ADC carries a first prize of PHP 500,000. The Jury hands down its award on January 15, and the period the Conditions allow for signing a design/build contract with the Owner lapses with no contract in place.

q: Who bears responsibility for drafting the ADC's full Conditions — its program, submission instructions, site plans, entry forms, and official envelopes and labels?
o: The Jury Chairman
The Professional Advisor
The IAPOA ADC Committee
The Owner's legal counsel
n: The Conditions (program, submission instructions, site plans, entry forms, official envelopes/labels) are drawn up by the Professional Advisor. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 2.7)

q: What does SPP Document 208 insist on when it comes to Jury meeting attendance?
o: A quorum of half the Jurors is enough for any meeting
Reserve Jurors may freely stand in for absent Jurors
All Jurors must be present at every Jury meeting
Only the Chairman is required to attend every meeting
n: It is essential that all Jurors be present at all meetings of the Jury. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.6)

q: Under what condition can the Owner make use of the first-prize design, and what rule covers every other entry submitted?
o: Any entry may be used freely
Only the top three may be used
Any design, if royalties are paid
Only by commissioning its author; others need consent
n: The design awarded first prize can only be used by the Owner upon his commissioning the Author to carry out the plan/design preparation for the project. No other plan/design may be used wholly or in part by the Owner except by agreement with the Author concerned. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 9.2)

q: Ahead of any official ADC announcement, what must the IAPOA's ADC Committee furnish the Owner with?
o: Written approval of the draft Conditions
A list of pre-approved competitors
A surety bond for the prizes
A copyright waiver for the winner
n: The IAPOA, through the ADC Committee, must send the Owner a written approval of the draft Conditions, including the timetable, the ADC registration fee (when required), and the composition of the Jury, before any official announcement. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 3.1)

q: In a two-stage format, who is meant to judge both rounds, and what must happen before a competition approved as single-stage can add a second stage?
o: Any Jury; the Owner alone approves
The same Jury; a second stage needs IAPOA approval
A new Jury; no second stage allowed
The Advisor picks a new Jury
n: In a two-stage competition, the same Jury should judge both stages. A competition approved as single-stage may proceed to a second stage only with IAPOA approval of the Conditions and of arrangements for payment of honoraria to the Competitors involved, over and above the original prize money; if a secondary competition takes place, the original Jury must be reappointed by the Owner. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.9)

q: Once Competitors have the ADC details in hand, what are they required to do, and what does that step signify?
o: Submit a preliminary sketch to the Professional Advisor, implying conditional participation
Register directly with the IAPOA ADC Committee, implying eligibility to sit on the Jury
Register with the Owner — registration implies acceptance of the ADC's Conditions
Pay the full registration fee to the Jury Chairman, which implies a binding contract for the project
n: As soon as they have received details of the ADC, all Competitors shall register with the Owner. Registration implies acceptance of the Conditions of the ADC. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 10.1)

q: In a National ADC, how must the Conditions and program of requirements be given out to competitors?
o: Issued only to competitors who reach the second stage
Adjustable individually if a competitor requests it
Allowed to vary depending on each competitor's qualifications
Identical for every competitor
n: The ADC conditions, including the program of requirements of a National ADC, shall be identical for all competitors. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.2)

q: What does the Jury owe in terms of making awards, and how must it handle the funds set aside for prizes?
o: Make final awards and use the full prize fund
Shift unused prizes to the Advisor's fee
Decline to award if no entry stands out
Award only one top prize
n: The Jury must make awards. The awards shall be final and made public by a date agreed on with the IAPOA and stated in the Conditions; the Jury, when distributing the awards, shall make full use of the amount set aside for prizes in the ADC Conditions. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.12)

q: Whose job is it to insure the Competitors' submitted plans/designs, and over what period does that duty extend?
o: IAPOA, from submission to exhibition
The Owner, while responsible for the entries
The Advisor, during deliberations only
The competitors themselves
n: The Owner shall insure the Competitors' plans/designs from the time when he assumes responsibility for them and for the duration of his responsibility. The amount of such insurance shall be stated in the Conditions. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 11.1)

q: What standard must information given to competitors (social, economic, technical, geographic, topographic, etc.) meet, and who can hand out supplementary data for a second-stage round?
o: Optional in limited competitions
Withheld until stage two; IAPOA issues it
Specific and clear; Owner issues approved supplements
General; the Advisor issues supplements
n: Information supplied to competitors must be specific and not open to misinterpretation. Supplementary information and instructions approved by the Jury may be issued by the Owner to Competitors selected to proceed to the second stage of a two-stage competition. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.5)

q: Apart from members of the Jury, who else is barred from entering the ADC or helping a Competitor with it?
o: Past winners of a national ADC
Any registered architect
Only foreign architects
Promoting-body members and ADC organizers
n: No member of the promoting body, nor any associate or employee, nor any person concerned with the preparation or organization of the ADC, will be eligible to compete or assist a Competitor. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 7.2)

q: Given the scenario, what becomes of drawings/plans that neither won a prize nor were purchased, and by what date must any required models go back to their Authors?
o: Destroyed; models returned within a month
Auctioned; models never returned
Kept; models returned within a year
Archived; models returned within a week
n: All drawings and plans, other than those which received prizes or were purchased and retained by the Owner, shall be destroyed at the end of the public exhibition, unless the Conditions provide otherwise. Where models are required, these will be returned to the Author/s at the expense of the Owner within a month of the close of the public exhibition. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 13.1)
scenario: Several Competitors submitted physical models along with their entries to an ADC, and the public exhibition of all entries wraps up on October 1.

q: How is the Professional Advisor's part in Jury deliberations correctly described?
o: He votes on procedural matters only, not on substantive ones
He assists the Jury and sits in on its deliberations, but has no vote
He is kept out of all Jury deliberations to preserve his neutrality
He presides over the Jury and breaks any tie vote
n: The Professional Advisor will assist the Jury and will be present during its deliberations but he will have no vote; his responsibilities are limited to the organization and conduct of the competition. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 5.1)

q: Given that announcement date, what is the latest date by which the Owner must pay out the prizes the Jury allotted?
o: June 1, three months after the announcement
March 8, one week after the announcement
April 1, one month after the announcement
There is no fixed deadline — payment may happen whenever suits the Owner
n: The Owner undertakes to accept the decisions of the Jury and to pay the prizes allotted within one (1) month of the official announcement of the ADC results — i.e., by April 1 if announced March 1. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.3)
scenario: The Owner of an ADC makes the competition's official results public on March 1.

q: When a dispute arises that has nothing to do with adjudication or the awarding of prizes, how is it to be resolved?
o: Through a re-vote by the original Jury
Through an immediate resort to the courts
Through a private settlement worked out between the Owner and the Professional Advisor
Through an arbitration process approved by the IAPOA, without first resorting to any form of litigation
n: In the event of a dispute not related to the adjudication process or awarding of the prizes, the matter shall be settled by an arbitration process approved by the IAPOA, and without initial recourse to any form of litigation. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 14.3)

q: Who selects the Jurors for an ADC, and what part does the IAPOA have in that selection?
o: The Owner appoints them, subject to IAPOA approval, with the IAPOA assisting the Owner in the selection
The Professional Advisor appoints them, ratified by the Competition Secretariat
The registered Competitors elect them
The IAPOA alone appoints them, with no Owner involvement
n: The Jurors are appointed by the Owner and approved by the IAPOA, which shall assist the Owner in the selection of the Jury members. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.2)

q: What are the Conditions required to spell out about how the Owner may use the winning design, and what statutes back this up?
o: The Owner may combine entries freely
Its intended use; no use or change without the author
Only IAPOA may permit its use
It enters the public domain once awarded
n: The Conditions shall state the use to which the Owner will put the winning plan/design; ADC-generated plans/designs may not be used or altered in any way except by agreement with the author. The Owner is not free to pick out portions of entries to compose another design — this is covered by ownership and copyright provisions under Secs. 20(4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004) and R.A. No. 8293 (IP Code) and their IRRs. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.6)

q: SPP Document 208 grounds copyright and ownership protection for ADC-generated designs in which specific statutes?
o: PD 1096, the Building Code
RA 9285, the ADR Act, alone
RA 9266 and RA 8293, with their IRRs
RA 386, the Civil Code, alone
n: Secs. 8.6 and 9.4 cite R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004, Secs. 20(4) and 33) and R.A. No. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines), and their respective IRRs, as the basis for ownership and copyright protection of ADC-generated plans/designs. (R.A. No. 9285 is instead cited as the basis for the ADR modes in Sec. 14.) (Source: SPP Document 208, Secs. 8.6 and 9.4)

q: What requirement, tied to Jury representation, is meant to keep the competition properly conducted?
o: The Professional Advisor must have a vote as a Juror
Every Juror must be a non-architect, to preserve impartiality
The Owner must chair the Jury
At least one of the Architect-Jurors must represent the IAPOA
n: To ensure correct conduct of the competition, at least one of the Architect-Jurors shall represent the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.4)

q: If, in an Ideas Competition, the Owner opts to use all or part of the winning scheme, what is supposed to happen?
o: The Owner should do so in collaboration with the Author, on terms the Author finds acceptable
The Owner must hold a second competition to pick an executing architect
The Owner may proceed on his own, since ideas carry no protection
The Owner must pay the IAPOA a penalty
n: In an Ideas Competition, if the Owner decides to make use of all or part of the winning scheme, he should do so with the collaboration of the Author; the terms of collaboration must be acceptable to the latter. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.9)

q: Within SPP Document 208, what does the phrase "SPP on ADC" designate?
o: The Jury's internal scoring rules
The Philippine SPP on design competitions
IAPOA's calendar of competitions
The Owner's own guidelines
n: "SPP on ADC" refers to the Philippine Standard of Professional Practice (SPP) on Architectural Design Competitions (ADC) itself. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 2.8)

q: At what point is each Juror supposed to review the ADC's Conditions?
o: Only if a particular Juror asks to see them
Only once entries have been submitted
Before the Conditions are released to Competitors
Simultaneously with the competitors, in the interest of fairness
n: Each Juror shall see the Conditions before they are made available to Competitors. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.7)

q: By default, how many times may the Owner execute the ADC-generated plan/design, and can that default be changed?
o: Never, without a separate license
Unlimited, unless the Conditions say no
Twice, once per stage
Once, unless the Conditions allow repeats
n: As a general rule, the Owner's right to use the ADC-generated plan/design covers one (1) execution only. However, the Conditions may provide for repetitive work and specify the terms thereof. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 9.3)

q: Who puts out the Notice of a National ADC, and what information must that notice carry?
o: The Owner or IAPOA Secretariat, noting approval
The Jury alone, with no approval note
The Advisor alone, naming every juror
The Secretariat, in the Gazette only
n: Notice of a National ADC is issued by the Owner and/or the IAPOA ADC Committee Secretariat, with a request for publication in technical journals or other media; the announcement must state where and how ADC documents may be obtained and that the Conditions have received the requisite IAPOA approval. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 3.2)

q: Before it reviews a Competitor's entry, what must the Jury do with any drawings, photographs, models, or documents that the rules don't call for?
o: Score them as bonus material
Exclude them before examining the entry
Forward them to the Owner for a separate look
Disqualify the whole entry automatically
n: Any drawings, photographs, models or other documents not required under the regulations shall be excluded by the Jury before it examines a Competitor's entry. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.10)

q: When the Owner conditions the release of competition documentation on a deposit, what happens to that deposit for a Competitor who submits a genuine plan/design?
o: It is donated to the IAPOA ADC Committee
It is forfeited to cover administrative costs
It is returned to them, unless stated otherwise
It goes toward that Competitor's registration fee for a future competition
n: The Owner shall issue to all Competitors the necessary documentation for preparing their plans/designs. Where furnishing such documentation is conditional on payment of a deposit, unless otherwise stated, such a deposit shall be returned to Competitors who submit a bona fide plan/design. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 10.2)

q: Sec. 4.3 requires a National ADC's Conditions to spell out everything below, EXCEPT:
o: The purpose of the ADC and the Owner's intentions
All the requirements a Competitor must meet
The nature of the problem the competition seeks to solve
The personal contact numbers of every Jury member
n: Sec. 4.3 requires the Conditions to clearly state the purpose of the ADC and intentions of the Owner, the nature of the problem to be solved, and all requirements competitors must meet — not personal contact details of Jurors. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.3.1-4.3.3)

q: Who is responsible for the Jury members' fees and their travel and subsistence expenses?
o: The Owner
The IAPOA ADC Committee
The Jury members, out of their own pocket
The Professional Advisor
n: The fees and travel and subsistence expenses of the Jury members shall be paid by the Owner. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.13)

q: Given that, how long must this exhibition generally run, and what must go along with it?
o: Thirty days, free only for architects
At least two weeks, free, with the jury report
No minimum; up to the Owner
One week, naming disqualified entrants
n: All designs, including those disqualified by the Jury, shall be exhibited, as a general rule, for at least two (2) weeks, together with a copy of the signed report of the Jury. The exhibition shall be open to the public free of charge. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 12.1)
scenario: Once the Jury has rendered its decision on an ADC, the Owner puts all the entries — disqualified ones included — on public exhibition.

q: What information must the Conditions provide about required documents, plans, or models, and what rule applies whenever a cost estimate is called for?
o: The Advisor decides format after submission
Only the deadline; no cost estimates
Number, scale and format of submissions
The Jury decides format after entries
n: The Conditions shall state the number, nature, scale and dimensions of the documents, plans or models required and the terms of acceptance of such documents or models; where an estimate of cost is required, the Conditions must prescribe a standard form of presentation. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.6)

q: What must the Conditions spell out about prizes, and what factors should the prize amounts track?
o: Only the project budget
Disclosed only after judging
Only the first prize
Number and amount, matched to the work involved
n: The Conditions must state the amount and number of prizes. The prizes awarded must be related to the size and complexity of the project, the amount of work involved, and the expense incurred by Competitors. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.1)

q: To anticipate possible disputes, what must the ADC Conditions provide for, and under what law are these dispute-resolution modes framed?
o: Conciliation, mediation, arbitration under RA 9285
Arbitration with the Owner as sole arbiter
Nothing; disputes go straight to court
A waiver of every legal remedy
n: Since no regulations, however well drawn up, can preclude the possibility of dispute, provisions for conciliation, mediation and arbitration — i.e., ADR modes under R.A. No. 9285 — must be included in the ADC Conditions and must precede any form of litigation. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 14.1)

q: Apart from drafting the Conditions, which task also falls to the Professional Advisor under SPP Document 208?
o: Judging technical merit of entries
Handling questions and entries, keeping anonymity
Approving the Jury's final report
Handing out the prizes
n: The Professional Advisor's function includes ensuring the ADC timetable is adhered to, supervising receipt of Competitors' questions, dispatch of replies to all Competitors, receipt of competition entries, and safeguarding the anonymity of Competitors at all times. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 5.1)

q: On top of the prizes awarded, what must every participant in a limited, invitation-only ADC also receive?
o: A certificate of participation, and nothing more
A guaranteed commission on some future project
An honorarium
Reimbursement of travel expenses, and nothing more
n: Each participant in a limited ADC by invitation shall receive an honorarium in addition to the prizes awarded. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.4)

q: When an ADC dispute goes to conciliation, mediation, or arbitration, who splits the resulting costs?
o: The Owner alone
The Jury members
IAPOA alone
The two parties, between themselves
n: The expenses resulting from any conciliation, mediation or arbitration procedure shall be shared by the two (2) interested parties to the ADR proceeding. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 14.4)

q: Given that choice, what is the ceiling on Jury size under SPP Document 208, and what minimum share of that Jury must be Architects?
o: Seven (7) members, with a majority — 4 of the 7 — being Architects
Five (5) members, with at least two (2) being Architects
Seven (7) members, with only one (1) needing to be an Architect
Nine (9) members, with at least five (5) being Architects
n: The Jury shall be composed of the smallest reasonable number of persons, in any event an odd number not exceeding seven (7); the majority of them — i.e., 4 out of 7 — shall be Architects. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.3)
scenario: For an ADC he is convening, an Owner opts to name the largest number of Jurors that SPP Document 208 permits.

q: When first prize in a Project ADC goes to a design, what does that obligate the Owner to do, and what happens if the winner can't convince the Jury he's capable of executing the work?
o: Pay only the prize money
Commission the author, with a partner if needed
The winner forfeits the prize
Rebid to another architect
n: In Project ADCs, the award of first prize to a plan/design places the Owner under an obligation to entrust the Author with the commission for the Project. If the winning Competitor is unable to satisfy the Jury of his ability to carry out the work, the Jury may require him to collaborate with another Architect of his choice, duly approved by the Jury and Owner. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 8.7)

q: Taken together, in which set of matters does SPP Document 208 show the IAPOA (via its ADC Committee) approving or getting involved?
o: Only the exhibition dates
Only disputes in litigation
Conditions, jury, advisor, second stage, disputes
Only the registration fee
n: Throughout the document, the IAPOA (through its ADC Committee, or NBD for the Professional Advisor) is involved in approving the draft Conditions (Sec. 3.1), assisting in Jury selection (Sec. 6.2), approving the Professional Advisor's appointment (Sec. 5.1), approving a single-stage competition's move to a second stage (Sec. 6.9), and approving the arbitration process for disputes not related to adjudication or prizes (Sec. 14.3). (Source: SPP Document 208, Secs. 3.1, 5.1, 6.2, 6.9, 14.3)

q: At most, how many representatives of the Owner may sit on the Jury?
o: Two (2)
Three (3), one for each stage
None — the Owner cannot have any representative on the Jury
One (1)
n: There should not be more than one (1) representative of the Owner included in the Jury. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.5)

q: Who keeps the copyright to a submitted plan/design, and what must happen before it can be altered in any way?
o: The author; changes need written consent
IAPOA, in trust for the Jury
Owner and author jointly
The Owner, upon submission
n: The Author of any plan/design shall retain the copyright of his work; no alterations may be made without his/her written consent. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 9.1)

q: Who names the IAPOA ADC Committee's members, and what is the Committee's job?
o: The Professional Advisor appoints it, to draft the Conditions
The IAPOA National President appoints it, to oversee every ADC referred to the IAPOA
The Owner appoints it, to judge entries directly
The Jury appoints it, to handle disputes
n: The IAPOA ADC Committee is appointed by the IAPOA National President to oversee all architectural design competitions (ADCs) referred to the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 2.9)

q: By what process does the Jury reach its decisions, and what takes place once the competition's awards are settled?
o: The Advisor's tie-breaking vote
Unanimous vote; no report
Majority vote; all jurors sign the report
The Owner ratifies the result
n: The decisions of the Jury shall be taken by a majority vote, with a separate vote on each competition plan/design submitted. The list of ADC awards, including the Jury's report to the Owner, shall be signed by all Jurors before the Jury is dissolved, and one copy of this document shall be sent to the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 6.8)

q: Absent a different rule in the Conditions, who holds the sole right to reproduce an ADC design, and on what legal footing?
o: The Professional Advisor
IAPOA, as custodian
The Owner, under the Civil Code
The author, under RA 9266
n: In all cases, unless otherwise stated in the Conditions, the Author of any design shall retain the sole right of reproduction by virtue of sole copyright under Secs. 20(4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and its IRR. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 9.4)

q: A Professional Advisor discovers that a competitor's identity has leaked to some Jurors before the final decision. Which SPP Document 208 principle has been breached?
o: The requirement that competitors' anonymity be preserved until final judgment
The rule that competitor registration follows a set process
The requirement that all competitors receive identical Conditions
The rule limiting the Jury to seven members
n: It is essential that the anonymity of competitors be maintained until the final judgment of the competition; rigorous measures should be taken to ensure this principle is observed. (Source: SPP Document 208, Sec. 4.1)
